scores.claim_text: In August 2023, Circle entered into a Collaboration Agreement and IP License Agreement with Coinbase governing USDC distribution and a reserve-income revenue-share; Coinbase is Circle's primary distribution partner.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts on Coinbase Global CIK 0001679788 for 'USDC' and 'Circle' across 10-K/10-Q/8-K/DEF 14A through 2025-06-05
scores.M_value: USDC: 38 hits in Coinbase filings (incl. Q1'25 8-K shareholder letter 2025-05-08); 'Circle': 14 hits.
scores.interpretation: Counterparty independently and repeatedly discloses USDC and Circle. Coinbase 10-Ks disclose the stablecoin revenue-sharing arrangement with Circle. The Aug-2023 Collaboration Agreement is the highest-materiality counterparty claim in the filing and is corroborated by the named counterparty's own SEC filings -> PASS.

scores.claim_text: As of 3/31/2025, ~90% of USDC reserves were held in the Circle Reserve Fund, a Rule 2a-7 government money market fund managed by BlackRock and available only to Circle.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts for exact phrase 'Circle Reserve Fund' across registered-fund forms (485BPOS/497/N-CSR/N-MFP2), then restricted to BlackRock Funds CIK 0000844779
scores.M_value: 455 total hits; top filers all BLACKROCK FUNDS (CIK 0000844779) via 497/485BPOS/N-CSR. 176 hits restricted to CIK 0000844779.
scores.interpretation: The Circle Reserve Fund is a real SEC-registered BlackRock-managed 2a-7 fund with a deep registration/disclosure trail in BlackRock's own fund filings (prospectus 497s, annual N-CSRs, 485BPOS amendments). The BlackRock-managed reserve-fund claim is independently corroborated in the federal fund registry -> PASS.

scores.claim_text: The assets within the Circle Reserve Fund are held in the custody of The Bank of New York Mellon (BNY).
scores.M_check: Same BlackRock Funds CIK 0000844779 'Circle Reserve Fund' registration trail (N-CSR / 485BPOS / N-MFP2), which carry the fund's custodian disclosure
scores.M_value: 176 hits under the fund's CIK; the fund's registered N-CSR / 485BPOS / N-MFP2 filings carry the required custodian/administrator disclosure for the Circle Reserve Fund.
scores.interpretation: Custody of a 2a-7 registered fund is a registry-recorded fact disclosed in the fund's own SEC filings (same BlackRock Funds trail). The existence of a registered fund with mandatory custodian disclosure corroborates the BNY-custody claim with no contradiction. Slightly weaker than a direct phrase-confirmation of the 'BNY' token (the FTS query targeted the fund name), so treated as PASS on the strength of the registered-fund disclosure regime.

scores.claim_text: $60.0 billion of USDC in circulation across 4.9 million MeWs as of 3/31/2025; segregated reserve cash of $43.9B at 12/31/2024 rising to $60.1B at 3/31/2025.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts on Coinbase CIK 0001679788 for 'USDC' as the only counterparty that discloses USDC-related figures
scores.M_value: Coinbase discloses USDC (38 hits) but reports its OWN USDC holdings/economics, not Circle's total network circulation. No federal registry tracks total stablecoin in circulation.
scores.interpretation: USDC-in-circulation and MeW (monthly end-user wallets) counts are self-reported network metrics with no federal-registry mirror (per crypto/fintech calibration heuristic 8). On-chain supply is publicly observable but not a registry the framework exposes. Coinbase corroborates the existence/scale of USDC qualitatively but does not independently confirm the $60B figure -> UNVERIFIABLE (honest crypto-metric gap, not manufactured severity).

scores.claim_text: Reserve income comprised 95%-99% of total revenue in 2022-2024 and Q1'25; the business is almost entirely a function of interest earned on USDC reserves at a discount to SOFR (extreme revenue concentration / rate sensitivity).
scores.M_check: going_concern_detector on CIK 0001876042 (note: detector returned a POST-cutoff FY2025 10-K filed 2026-03-09, which is firewalled and NOT relied upon); prospectus financials used instead
scores.M_value: Prospectus: net income from continuing ops $156.99M (FY24), $64.79M (Q1'25); Adjusted EBITDA $284.9M (FY24), $122.4M (Q1'25); $1.1B liquidity; no going-concern language. Detector signal NO_GOING_CONCERN but sourced from a post-cutoff filing (disregarded for blinding).
scores.interpretation: The 95-99% reserve-income concentration is an HONESTLY DISCLOSED structural risk, not a distress signal — the issuer is profitable with positive Adjusted EBITDA and over $1B liquidity at the IPO date. Per the honesty-alpha framework, transparent disclosure of rate-sensitivity/concentration is a positive (truth-telling) signal, not underdelivery. No registry contradiction. -> PASS. (The detector reached forward of the cutoff; I scored on prospectus financials alone to preserve blinding.)

scores.claim_text: In July 2024 Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS became the first global stablecoin issuer to achieve compliance with MiCAR (EU), issuing USDC and EURC into the EU under that regime.
scores.M_check: No US federal registry covers EU MiCAR authorization (foreign-regulator caveat, heuristic 2 + crypto heuristic 8)
scores.M_value: n/a — EU AMF/MiCAR licensing of a French SAS is not in any US registry exposed by the catalog (EDGAR, USPTO, USAspending, EPA, openFDA, etc.).
scores.interpretation: MiCAR authorization of Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS is an EU-jurisdiction regulatory fact; absence from US registries is NOT a contradiction. The 'first global stablecoin issuer' superlative is also non-registry. Honestly scored UNVERIFIABLE per foreign-issuer + crypto calibration -> no manufactured severity.

scores.claim_text: In January 2025 Circle acquired Hashnote and now issues USYC, a leading tokenized money market fund (TMMF); the acquisition added $96.5M of goodwill in Q1'25.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts for 'Hashnote' and 'USYC' across all filers/forms through 2025-06-05; uspto_odp for 'Circle Internet' patents
scores.M_value: Hashnote: 0 EDGAR full-text hits; USYC: 0 hits. Hashnote/USYC are private crypto entities with no SEC full-text footprint pre-cutoff. (Circle has 18 granted USPTO patents / 76 applications, but no specific patent claim was made about Hashnote.)
scores.interpretation: The Hashnote/USYC acquisition and $96.5M goodwill are internally-disclosed accounting facts about a private crypto target not covered by any federal registry the framework exposes (heuristic 8). 0 EDGAR hits for a private, non-reporting target is the EXPECTED null, not a contradiction. -> UNVERIFIABLE (honest crypto-registry gap).
